intuition: One could collect values in a set and build a replacement list, but the task asks for direct edits to an existing sorted chain. Sorted order makes the key observation simple: every repeated value occurs in one consecutive run. Keeping one representative of each run does not require remembering earlier values.

Let current be that representative. If its successor has the same value, bypass the successor by connecting current to the node after it. Do not advance current yet: another equal node may follow. When the successor differs, the current run is finished, and current can move forward to represent the next run.

Each iteration either removes one duplicate or advances past one retained node, so the procedure finishes after linear work. An empty list needs no special allocation, and a singleton already meets the requirement. Distinguish this problem from removing every value that has duplicates: here a repeated run still leaves exactly one node. The returned head remains the original first node when the input is nonempty.

steps: For [1,1,2,3,3], current starts at the first 1.
Its successor is also 1, so current.next skips that duplicate and now points to 2.
The next value differs; advance current to 2, then to the first 3.
The successor 3 matches, so bypass it without moving the representative.
No successor remains. Return the original head with values [1,2,3].

codeNotes.note: Bypass an equal node while preserving the representative and the rest of the chain.
Advance only after adjacent values differ, ensuring longer duplicate runs are fully removed.

codeNotes.code: while current is not None and current.next is not None:
codeNotes.note: The guard handles empty lists and guarantees both compared nodes exist.
